questions.q: How does this lesson describe the structure of the Salesforce Certified System Architect credential?
options: A single standalone exam, unrelated to any other Salesforce certification
A multi-exam, overlay-style credential, awarded once a candidate holds a defined set of individual architecture certifications simultaneously in active status
A credential earned automatically after one year of Salesforce administration experience
A credential that requires no other certifications of any kind
questions.explain: The lesson describes System Architect as an overlay credential: rather than one exam, a candidate earns a defined set of individual certifications, and the overlay credential is awarded once that full set is held simultaneously.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does the System Architect track's overlay structure tell you about the nature of System Architecture as a discipline?
options: That it is a single, simple skill that can be tested in one short exam
That System Architecture is a named combination of several distinct architecture competencies, each substantial enough to be certified on its own
That it has no relationship to integration, identity, or deployment topics
That it is identical in every respect to the Application Architect track
questions.explain: The lesson draws the conclusion that the overlay structure reflects System Architecture being a combination of several distinct, individually substantial competencies rather than one monolithic skill.

questions.q: Which domain does this lesson connect to Lesson 18's content on release management, sandbox strategy, and environment planning?
options: Data Architecture
Sharing and Visibility Architecture
Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architecture
Marketing Automation Architecture
questions.explain: The lesson connects Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architecture specifically to the release management, sandbox strategy, and environment planning material covered in Lesson 18.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the difference in emphasis between the System Architect and Application Architect tracks?
options: There is no difference -- the two tracks are functionally identical

Application Architecture leans toward how a single Salesforce implementation is designed internally (data model, sharing, visibility), while System Architecture leans toward how Salesforce fits into and interacts with everything around it
System Architecture only covers security, while Application Architecture covers everything else
Application Architecture is only relevant to non-profit organizations
questions.explain: The lesson describes Application Architecture's emphasis as internal design (data model, sharing, visibility) versus System Architecture's emphasis on integration, cross-system identity, and release/environment strategy -- echoing the distinction Lesson 1 opened the course with.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a candidate should do before registering for any exam in the System Architect track?
options: Rely entirely on this lesson's description without checking anything further
Confirm the current prerequisite exams, question format, passing score, and fee directly on Salesforce's own official certification pages, since third-party sources can be outdated or conflicting
Assume all third-party blog posts about the exam are equally reliable and current
Skip the prerequisite exams entirely, since they are optional
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that exam details are controlled by Salesforce and change over time, with even recent third-party sources disagreeing on specifics -- so the responsible step is confirming current details directly on Salesforce's own certification pages before registering.
